changelog: Replace C5 to give constructive guidance for dense cuts in low-latency regimes rather than a blanket prohibition on cutting near heads; this addresses the finding that head-avoidance was over-applied and harms short-latency pairs.

Insert a new principle after C8 that forces low ranking for cuts whose standalone contradiction probability is high unless adjacent kept cuts will reliably restore context; this addresses the primary finding that entailment risk was underweighted when cohesion looked good.

Replace C5 to address over-broad head-avoidance: allow denser safe cuts in very-low-latency regimes and give constructive guidance (require high cohesion and absence of high-contra single cuts; prefer cuts after complete constituents).
Replace E1 with labeled example en_us_48 to teach the scorer about high-contra single cuts that kill set quality (addresses the primary finding that entailment risk is underweighted).
Replace E2 with labeled example en_us_1081 to illustrate a ≤5-bin case where a single high-contra cut must be ranked low despite apparent cohesion (covers mid-low latency loss).
Replace E4 with labeled example en_us_455 to show another ≤3-bin instance where keeping a cohesive-looking but highly-contradictory cut harms overall set score.

Insert a concise low-latency guidance unit after C5: allow denser safe cuts in ≤3/≤5 regimes by preferring cuts that end on complete constituents and have high cohesion and low standalone contradiction; avoid treating 'avoid heads' as an absolute ban. This directly addresses the primary finding about over-broad head-avoidance.
